recommendations.abstract: We introduce FormCraft, a framework for representing acquired operations as first-class capabilities that can be recursively composed, directly invoked, and selectively retained in a persistent library through domain-specific verification. The framework separates capability well-formedness and public callability from later admission to persistent storage while preserving formation provenance and operational identity. We formalize recursive compositional closure over a uniform capability space and show that formed composites can be reused through the same public interface without re-forming their historical derivation. Experiments across continuous, discrete, propositional, and sequence domains demonstrate instance-independent reuse, independent checking, persistent acquisition, and reduced reuse-time search work under first-class exposure.

contribution.en: FormCraft represents acquired operations as first-class capabilities that can be recursively composed and persistently reused.
contribution.zh: FormCraft将习得操作表示为可递归组合、可持久复用的第一类能力。

why_care.en: Compositional capability reuse and verification relate to program synthesis and IR library learning.
why_care.zh: 组合能力复用与验证关联程序合成和IR库学习。

recommendations.title: Recursive Formation and First-Class Reuse of Compositional Capabilities

recommendations.abstract: Lane-based RISC-V vector processors exploit data parallelism well but pay a recurring cost for two common patterns: reductions, which require a separate tree pass, and deep dependent expression chains, which cannot be fused and are issued as serial vector instructions. We present TALU, a 5-stage RISC-V core whose execute stage is an NxN grid of registered ALU tiles instead of a single ALU. The grid is a reconfigurable, feed-forward spatial fabric: tiles route operands only from non-backward neighbours, and added diagonal forwarding lets a reduction collapse spatially. A minimal custom extension configures the per-tile operation, routing, and per-tile constants, and streams operands through the array. On a single fabric, TALU runs ordinary scalar code, single deep-path expressions, and multi-lane vector kernels. On the benchmark suite of the RISC-V2 vector processor, TALU is 1.8-5.5x faster than RISC-V2 and 4.5-15.5x faster than Vicuna at equal lane count, with a reduction cost (dot{\div}add) of 1.05x versus 1.96x and 1.26x for the vector cores. A retimed implementation places and routes at 1.03 GHz in 45 nm in 0.30 mm2, half the area of RISC-V2.

contribution.en: Introduces TALU, a RISC-V core replacing the execute-stage ALU with an NxN reconfigurable ALU tile grid to accelerate reductions and deep dependent expression chains.
contribution.zh: 提出TALU，一种用NxN可配置ALU tile网格替换单ALU执行级的RISC-V核，加速归约和深依赖表达式链。

why_care.en: Relates to SIMD/vectorization, heterogeneous architecture, and compiler-architecture co-design, potentially influencing instruction selection and vector code generation.
why_care.zh: 与SIMD/向量化、异构架构和编译-架构协同相关，可能影响指令选择与向量代码生成。

recommendations.title: TALU: A Reconfigurable Tiled-ALU Grid for RISC-V

recommendations.abstract: Sparse matrices, in which most entries are zero, are central to scientific simulation, graph analytics and machine learning, and their multiplication with dense inputs is a core parallel kernel. In many applications the matrix stays fixed while only a few input rows change per step, so the result can be updated from those rows alone, which we call the dirty set. Sparse kernels often add a second optimization based on the inspector-executor principle, in which a tiled schedule is prepared once and reused across calls. However, when this reuse remains profitable as the dirty set moves is not well characterized. In this paper, we show that retained tiled execution rarely beats direct CSC in incremental sparse matrix multiplication, although incremental execution itself remains highly profitable. Across 21 SuiteSparse matrices and controlled patterns of motion, a direct column-wise incremental update is 2.1-8.2x faster than the best of eight full-recomputation codes, among them Intel oneMKL and PyTorch. Yet the same direct update outperforms a tiled executor that retains tile preparation and caches assembled schedules in 779 of 837 workloads. Separating reuse into per-tile preparation and cached schedules shows that the benefit comes from preparation; extra cache capacity seldom helps because a tile set rarely returns after a different one has intervened. Tiling is faster only when tiles merge many entries into each output write, a structural property that we predicted before measurement and confirmed on four held-out matrices of the same family. These results show that the structure of the matrix and the motion of the dirty set, rather than the sophistication of the schedule, determine whether reuse is profitable. We anticipate that our methodology and guidelines will help developers decide when to build schedule reuse into incremental sparse runtimes.

contribution.en: Characterizes incremental sparse matrix multiplication and finds retained tiled schedule reuse rarely beats direct CSC updates.
contribution.zh: 刻画增量稀疏矩阵乘法，发现保留的分块调度复用很少优于直接CSC更新。

why_care.en: Challenges assumptions about inspector-executor schedule reuse, informing compiler and runtime decisions for incremental sparse kernels.
why_care.zh: 挑战了inspector-executor调度复用的假设，为增量稀疏内核的编译器和运行时决策提供依据。

recommendations.title: How the Dirty Set Moves: Characterizing Schedule Reuse in Incremental Sparse Matrix Multiplication
